 Marvel Studios has been revealing more of the MCU's history in VisionQuest , fundamentally changing what we thought we knew about Tony Stark's Iron Man timeline. Robert Downey Jr.'s portrayal of Stark has carried the character well for over a decade. And while he hasn't appeared in VisionQuest in the flesh, his legacy has had a huge impact on Marvel's latest Disney+ series. Terry Matalas' series follows the artificial intelligences Tony Stark created in the MCU, but it has revealed they weren't Stark's design at all.

 While Paul Bettany's Vision and James Spader's Ultron have taken center stage in VisionQuest , the series has also spotlighted several other new and intriguing artificial intelligences. We had met JARVIS (James D'Arcy), FRIDAY (Orla Brady), EDITH (Emily Hampshire), DUM-E (Henry Lewis), and U (Jonathan Sayer) before in AI form, but the likes of the tactical Handler (Diane Morgan) and Jocasta (T'Nia Miller) are incredible new additions. The latter has changed everything we knew about AI in the MCU.
 Tony Stark's VisionQuest Connection Changes What We Knew About Iron Man
 Image via Paramount/Courtesy Everett Collection 
 Tony Stark introduced audiences to the MCU back in 2008, becoming the franchise's first on-screen superhero, Iron Man, following his experiences under Ten Rings captivity in Afghanistan. When Stark returned home, he turned to his trusty artificial intelligence, JARVIS, to help refine the Iron Man suit's design and run his home, arsenal, and robotics.
 Without JARVIS, it's hard to imagine Tony Stark ever becoming Iron Man, and we were led to believe that Stark himself had designed and built the AI. JARVIS, standing for Just Another Rather Very Intelligent System, was inspired by Howard Stark's (Dominic Cooper and John Slattery) butler and trusty friend, Edwin Jarvis (D'Arcy in Avengers: Endgame) .
 Fans assumed, when Iron Man was released, that Tony Stark had been using JARVIS for years before the movie, since they were so familiar. However, VisionQuest has now revealed that this is indeed not the case. In fact, it seems that Stark purchased the AI that would become JARVIS only shortly before Iron Man .
 VisionQuest revealed that biological-technology company Markridge Biotech, not Stark Industries, carried out groundbreaking research that cracked the code on non-human artificial general intelligence. Markridge was comprised of five researchers: Simon Moorhouse (Art Malik), Rebecca Edwards (Joanne Randle), Richard Gaines, Katerina Wells (Mary McDonnell), and Josephine Carrington (Miller).
 Together, they developed the Proto-One artificial intelligence by combining Phineas Horton's original AI source code, which helped him develop the Synthetic Man, JIM (Bettany), and Carrington's own brain scan. Tony Stark purchased Proto-One and all other intellectual property when Stark Industries acquired Markridge Biotech after Jo Carrington's death in 2008.
 This means Stark acquired Proto-One only in 2008, perhaps mere months before the events of the first Iron Man movie. Changing this part of Stark's timeline forces us to reconsider more of his MCU backstory, even though he stood on the shoulders of giants to forge a greater legacy in artificial intelligence.
 VisionQuest Forces Us to Reconsider a Lot of Tony Stark's Backstory
 Stills from VisionQuest Image via Marvel Studios 
 While the revelation that Tony Stark didn't design JARVIS is certainly interesting, it could also be game-changing for the MCU. It seems Tony Stark's entire MCU timeline has changed , as much of what we thought we knew about the genius, billionaire, playboy, and philanthropist may not be true .
 Sure, the code for Proto-One was sold to Stark before Carrington's death, but only shortly before the events of Iron Man , meaning Stark must have quickly rejigged the code into JARVIS. Beyond revealing JARVIS's history, VisionQuest also spotlights the synthetic robot Jocasta, adapted from the Marvel Comics character Ultron created as his bride.
 Interestingly, Jocasta and Ultron's bodies in VisionQuest have strikingly similar designs, even though Markridge Biotech designed the former and Ultron forged the latter from Tony Stark's Iron Legion designs. VisionQuest also confirms that Stark was not the first to implement nanotechnology, as Markridge did as well.
 Before Jo Carrington's death, she envisioned a world in which every human had an artificially intelligent nanobot implanted in their body, acting as an internal doctor, companion, and guide. Tony Stark's nanotech suits were treated as the pinnacle of his personal innovation in Avengers: Infinity War and Endgame. 
 However, Markridge seems to have gotten there first, engineering billions of microscopic machines now held in the "nest" at Carrington's grave. Stark would have acquired this tech when buying Markridge in 2008. As it turns out, everything Tony Stark had in the first Iron Man movie, he poached, bought, upgraded, and refined from Markridge Biotech.
 For the last 18 years, audiences have been led to believe that Stark was a singular genius who created all this technological magic, but he was actually working with secondhand knowledge and resources, first brought to life by Markridge. Even so, Stark still showed genius and innovation, doing something even Markridge couldn't have imagined.
 Tony Stark Still Succeeded Where Other AI Pioneers Failed
 Stills from VisionQuest Image via Marvel Studios 
 Markridge Biotech may have built the framework for artificial general intelligence in the MCU, but Tony Stark refined that foundation and gave each of his AIs distinct personalities.
 VisionQuest revealed that each of these AIs was based on real people from Stark's history, including Alison Hogan (Brady), Howard Stark's secretary who helped raise Tony, Edith Marks (Hampshire), a fighter pilot and Howard Stark's personal crash-test dummy whose husband died in a plane crash, and even Edwin Jarvis himself.
 Even Markridge couldn't do this, but instead somehow uploaded Jo Carrington's entire consciousness into Jocasta's synthetic body , rather than building an AI based on her. This is what sets Tony Stark apart from Markridge, as he didn't butcher a human to develop his AI. Instead, he took the framework Markridge built and manually shaped it to mirror the warmth and presence of his foundational figures.
 Stark created something beautiful out of something sterile. This is clearest in Vision himself . Phineas Horton's original Synthetic Man burst into flames, destroying his home, his creator, and himself when he felt too much emotion. However, Vision can fully embrace his most human tendencies and feelings.
